1.note: "Short of hand" is read as poverty (Isa 50:2, 59:1 use it of power). "Shrinks in his pain" follows the usual reading of Job 6:10, a word with no other occurrence in the Bible.

2.note: Jer 4:30 "you tear (widen) your eyes with kohl". The edition points מֹרְךָ as "your myrrh", that is, the fragrance of his words. The image is uncertain.

3.note: The edition prints a full stop after עמוד, so "always" goes with the second half-line: "and always with our pen we adorn the kingship".

4.note: Read as "from drawing near to me" (compare Isa 65:5 קְרַב אֵלֶיךָ). A reading "from battle with me" (קְרָב, battle) is also possible.

5.note: "His parting" can be Time's or Ḥever's: Time parted them. The next line puns on חֶבֶר (Ḥever) and חֶבְרָתוֹ (his company).
